tests.test_edgeThe 17 TD-CDMA edge-case scenarios of chapter 8 on the numpy air, with random receive counters and link delays, checking that no two stations ever overlapThis review, all 17 scenarios (short versions): 93 of 93 checks, including a new one: a fragment its sender repeats while the first copy still waits at a relay is passed on once.
tests.test_fake_antsdr12 scenarios with every station the real app on cdma_phy.grc and emulated ANTSDRs (about 30 min at 0.4× real time)55 of 58 checks; the failures are real time on 2 cores (scenario 10)
tests.test_grc_flowgraph, test_grc_goodputCompile and run cdma_phy_sim.grc: every modulation and code rate, unicast and broadcast, three stations at once, a 6 dB channel; 100 KB through flowgraph and MAC, FEC on and offpass with GNU Radio 3.10.9.2; on a busy 2-core PC the 6 dB step can lose a frame
tests.test_grc_cores, test_tdma_phyThe flowgraph's Python cores with the stock blocks imitated in numpy, numpy-PHY ↔ GRC-PHY interoperability; bursts on exact samples, receive indices, D under drift, underrunspass; the timing base 19 of 19 checks
tests.test_ldpc, test_modem, test_profiles, test_bigfileLDPC (all 51 lifting sizes, rate matching, AWGN curves) and Golay; PHY impairments, false alarms, multi-user, collisions; every modulation and code rate; a 1 MB file at 14 dBpass; a 1 MB file at 14 dB: 178 kb/s on 16-QAM ¾, no retransmission
tests.test_link, test_powerThe MAC over the simulated air with spread ALOHA (concurrency, priority, a lossy link); power control's loop, the blocks carrying each burst's power, near-far with and without itpass; power control 18 of 18 checks (the blocks and the loop)
tests.test_uno, test_games, test_featuresEvery UNO rule and 300 random games; a UNO round, a player leaving and a race over the air; profile pictures, cancelling from either end, clock offsetspass; 300 random UNO games (108 cards every time); a 3-station UNO round and race
tests.ui_games, ui_featuresPlaywright drives every station's page: UNO, a race and a rematch, chat and the dashboard during the race, a page reload mid-race; themes, wallpaper editor, media quality, cancel, late messages, sounds, camera, the + traypass; 65 of 65 chat checks; UNO, race and rematch on 3 pages, the reloaded page carried on at its distance
tests.test_gr_backend, scenario_apiThe numpy PHY's GNU Radio backend against a stand-in GNU Radio; a full app scenario through the web APIpass (the API scenario now waits until the stations have heard each other)

10.5 Measured performance

WhatResultWhere
LDPC alone, BPSK, 1 KB framesRate ½: no frame error in 20 at Eb/N0 1.5 dB; ¾ at 2.5 dB; ⅚ at 3.5 dB. Uncoded needs about 10.5 dB.test_ldpc
Full receiver, Es/N0 for ~100 % of 1 KB framesQPSK ½ about 5 dB (the preamble detector's limit), ¾ 5.5, ⅚ 6; 16-QAM ½ 9, ⅔ 10, ¾ 11, ⅚ 12.5; uncoded 16-QAM 20–22 dB. The receiver's own accuracy limits it at about 44 dB.test_profiles
Robustness of the receiver3 s of noise on two codes: no false detection. Two links at once, the interferer 10 dB stronger: both decoded. Two senders overlapping at one receiver: 20 of 20 bursts. CFO ±12 kHz and a 20 ppm clock: QPSK ½ 10 of 12 frames at 4 dB, 11 of 12 at 6 dB.test_modem
One link, big files (spread ALOHA)2 MB at 28 dB: 236 kb/s, uncoded 16-QAM, no retransmission. 1 MB at 14 dB: 176–178 kb/s with LDPC (16-QAM ¾) against 37 kb/s uncoded (BPSK), 4.8 times as fast. 10 MB at 28 dB: 235 kb/s, intact.test_bigfile
The same with TD-CDMAOne 2 MB transfer: 190 kb/s, about 80 % of ALOHA (the receiver's slot, the join slot and the headers take their share). Four senders at once on radios that are deaf while they send: 173–181 kb/s together, against ALOHA's 53–58.test_edge 7
GNU Radio flowgraph, simulated channelEvery modulation and code rate through the stock soft decoders, the LDPC Decoder and the CRC-32 check; three stations at the same instant, 16-QAM ½ included, at 12 dB; 100 KB at 12 dB: 37.8 kb/s with adaptive LDPC against 15.6 kb/s uncoded (at 1 MS/s, a quarter of the radio rate).test_grc_flowgraph, test_grc_goodput

10.6 A ten-minute demonstration

  1. The PHYWalk through grc/cdma_phy.grc in GNU Radio Companion, then run cdma_phy_concept.grc (F6) to show despreading with the right and the wrong code.
  2. Bring-upStart the four stations with run (the grcc compile shows in the console). On the dashboard's Time slots panel: the slot plan, every station's measured D and its clock against the lead's in ppm.
  3. Text, ACK, addressingAlice → Bob: the ticks go 🕒 → ✓ → ✓✓ (the ACK rode in Bob's next header) and turn blue when Bob reads it. Carol's dashboard shows none of these frames: they are on code 2.
  4. CDMA inside a slotAlice sends Bob a photo and Carol a voice note at once while Dave sends Alice a file: Alice's slot carries both transfers on codes 2 and 3, the busy slots grow to about 100 ms and shrink a second after.
  5. Errors, priority, encryptionRaise --tx-atten or move an antenna: CRC drops and retransmissions, the image still intact. Send an ⚡ urgent text behind a large image: it arrives first. Restart a station with another --key: the UI warns.
  6. Adaptive coding, big filesA multi-MB file Alice → Bob at "16-QAM uncoded (258 kb/s)"; move Bob's antenna away step by step and watch the rate step down; restart with --fec off at 12–14 dB to see the coding gain.
  7. Groups, relaying, leavingA photo to Everyone counts 1/3, 2/3, ✓✓. Put Carol where Alice can't hear her: "via Bob". Close Dave's app (his slot is freed), then the lead's during a transfer (the next station takes over and the transfer goes on).
  8. GamesFour-player UNO (each screen shows only its own hand), then a race; take one station off the air for 10 s: UNO pauses with a countdown, the race shows a ghost, both carry on when it is back. V switches the chase camera.

10.7 Troubleshooting

SymptomCauseFix
grcc not found, or a compile error at startGNU Radio missing, or the .grc was edited into an invalid stateInstall GNU Radio 3.10+; open the file in GRC to see the red blocks, or restore the shipped one.
No module named gnuradio.iiogr-iio missingInstall it; iio_info -u ip:192.168.1.10 must list the device.
No stations appearDevice unreachable, different carriers or flowgraph variablesCheck iio_info, --freq and the .grc on every PC; another station's burst shows as a ~2.7 MHz hump in the dashboard spectrum.
High Eb/N0 but many CRC dropsSamples are being lost, not the radio linkTX underruns climbing: --tx-buffer 262144, close heavy programs. RX overflows climbing: the PC can't keep up (see below).
"header CRC-8 fails" climbing, few framesSNR too low (a few per burst of another station are normal)Raise --rx-gain, lower --tx-atten, move closer; lower the gain if the spectrum is clipped.
"LDPC decode failures" climbingThe link is below what its modulation needsWith --fec auto the sender steps down by itself; a forced --mod/--fec can't. More than 8 iterations on average means the link is at the edge.
rx_overflow_chunks, late bursts climbingThe PC is overloaded: the despreader's queue passed 3 s, or bursts reached the radio after their slot beganClose other programs; one station per PC with 4+ cores; as a last resort samp_rate = 2e6 in the .grc on every station.
"D jumps", "receiver search: everywhere"An underrun or a lost RX buffer moved the TX → RX offsetIt is measured again within a few slots; if frequent, raise --tx-buffer.
Two dashboards say lead stationTwo groups that don't hear each other's headersA station that hears both joins them; otherwise move stations closer or lower --tx-atten.
"Another station is using address N"Two stations with the same --idGive every station its own address.
The microphone doesn't workBrowsers block it on plain-HTTP remote addressesUse http://localhost, or attach an audio file.

10.8 Where everything is, and who owns it

PathWhat it holds
grc/The three flowgraphs (10.3); build/grc/ holds grcc's output, rebuilt at every start.
wavelink/config.py, codes.pyPHY parameters and the address → code mapping; Gold codes, preamble patterns, RRC taps.
modem.py, ldpc.py, nr_bg1.py, golay.pyThe numpy PHY (burst modulator and multi-code demodulator); 5G NR LDPC (lifting, encoder, rate matching, interleaver, layered min-sum decoder) and its base graph table; the Golay (24,12) header code.
grc_phy.py, radio_*.py, fake_antsdr.pyCompiling and attaching the .grc and the cores of its Embedded Python blocks; the numpy-PHY GNU Radio graph, the channel simulator and the radio interface; the emulated ANTSDR blocks and air.
mac.py, tdma.pyThe link layer (fragments, ARQ, adaptive modulation and coding, priority, power control, spread ALOHA) and the time slots (lead, plan, joining, takeover, D, link tables, relaying).
node.py, crypto.py, games/The application layer (envelope, groups, receipts, presence, profiles, clock offsets, history); AES-256-GCM; the game center (hub.py), UNO rules (uno.py) and the race packet (race.py).
wavelink/web/The stdlib HTTP + Server-Sent Events server and the browser app: chat, settings, wallpaper editor, media sheets and recorder, emoji, sounds, music, dashboard, game center, UNO and the race.
tools/make_grc.py and epy/ (the flowgraphs and their blocks), gen_nr_bg1.py, render_grc.py, make_logo.py, gen_emoji.py.
tests/The suites of 10.4, plus test_tx_underrun (mid-burst underruns per TX buffer size).

A split for a team of four: A, PHY DSP and coding (codes.py, modem.py, ldpc.py, golay.py, BER/FER measurements, gain tuning); B, GNU Radio and hardware (grc/cdma_phy.grc, grc_phy.py, ANTSDR firmware and addresses, the mid-evaluation tx/rx); C, the link layer (mac.py, tdma.py, ARQ, the modulation table, power control, the simulators); D, application and UI (node.py, web/, games/, encryption, dashboard, the demo script).

11

Known bugs and open issues

Bugs found during testing and already fixed are not listed. What is left is one open problem, the CPU load in real time, and limitations of the design that are known and bounded:

Open

Real time overloads a 2-core PC

Two stations and the emulated air on one 2-core VM in real time: 358 TX underruns, 124 lost RX buffers, the second station never got into the plan and a file failed. A receiving station needs about 2.1 cores, 1.6 of them Python under one interpreter lock.

WorkaroundOne station per PC, 4 or more cores, little else running. The real fix is future improvement 1.

Limitation

Slots can overlap for a cycle or two while two networks merge

When two networks meet, the slots of the one that yields can overlap the other's until its stations have joined. Inside a formed network slots never overlap.

WorkaroundStart stations within range of each other; the overlap lasts one or two cycles.

Limitation

A message of a few kilobytes waits 1.4 s with three or four stations

An idle slot (29.5 ms with three stations, 22 ms with four) is shorter than one full 1,023-byte frame even at the fastest rate (33.2 ms), so a message with a full fragment sends nothing until the sender's slot has grown, about 1.4 s later. With two stations (44 ms slots) a full frame fits at 16-QAM ⅚ or uncoded, and a message of one or two fragments takes the slowest rate that still fits the slot.

ImpactA 2 KB text or a small photo arrives about 1.4 s later than it could (1.5 instead of 0.2 s). Future improvement 13.

Limitation

A relayed transfer starts 2–5 s late

The relay's slot grows only after the sender's: plan changes go one at a time, each announced at least 1 s ahead, and the lead waits up to 1 s for the wishes of a station it can't hear. Meanwhile the sender's ACK timer runs out and it repeats what is in flight; the relay passes each fragment on once and drops the copies.

ImpactA relayed 30 KB file takes about 6.1 s in the simulator, against 2.1 s directly, and up to 18 s right after other transfers. Future improvement 14.

Limitation

UNO: the last move can be lost at a host handover

The next host carries on from the last table copy it received, so a move the old host accepted but never sent out is lost.

ImpactThe player repeats the move; rare, needs the host to drop off the air at that instant.

Limitation

UNO: hidden hands are in every station's memory

The table copy that makes host handover possible stays in the station and never reaches the browser, but a player who reads the station's memory could see the other hands.

ImpactCheating needs debugging tools on your own PC.

Limitation

On the flowgraph, game messages wait behind file frames

The code lanes are first-in first-out, so a UNO view can wait behind a window of file frames for up to 0.6 s. The host merges views that pile up, so no event is lost.

ImpactSlower moves during a big transfer to that player.

Limitation

Message order after a clock jump

The clock-offset estimate keeps the smallest delay of the last 5 minutes, so for a few minutes after a station's clock jumps its messages can be placed off by up to the jump.

WorkaroundRun NTP on the lab PCs.

Limitation

The CRC-drop counter is an estimate on the GNU Radio PHY

The stock CRC32 block drops bad frames silently, so the dashboard counts despread frames minus delivered frames.

ImpactDashboard only.

Limitation

Race updates slow down during file transfers

One car state per cycle: 10 a second at 100 ms, 4.7 at 213 ms and 2.4 at 415 ms while every station sends. Dead reckoning hides most of it.

ImpactRemote cars are less exact during transfers.

Limitation

The three-station GNU Radio simulation is CPU-bound

grc-sim runs three PHYs in one Python process at 1 MS/s; on 2 cores its 6 dB test step loses a frame in some runs and its file goodput halves.

ImpactTest environment only.

Limitation

Detection limits the low end

Coded QPSK ½ would decode at ~1.5 dB, but the 48-symbol preamble is only found reliably from ~4 dB.

ImpactAbout 3 dB of range left unused.

Untested

Not yet run on physical ANTSDRs

The analog front end (AGC, IQ imbalance, DC offset, phase noise, multipath), the real self-leak level and the E200's Ethernet jitter are not modelled, and power control has only run in simulators.

First lab sessionWatch for "TX->RX offset jumped", "radio stream gap" and late bursts; tune --rx-gain and --tx-atten.

12

Future improvements

1 · C++ blocks for the hot paths

Move the despreader's search and tracking and the Burst Combiner into out-of-tree C++ blocks. That removes most of the 1.6 cores of Python, makes real time possible on 2-core PCs, and would allow about 10 MS/s.

2 · Incremental redundancy

HARQ type II: on a failure send more parity of the same codeword (5G redundancy versions 1–3, already in the circular buffer) and combine it softly with what arrived, instead of resending the whole frame.

3 · A longer preamble

96 symbols instead of 48 would find bursts about 3 dB lower, close to where coded QPSK ½ decodes, at the cost of airtime and detector CPU.

4 · RAKE receiver

Two or three fingers for large rooms where delay spreads approach a chip; it matters most for 16-QAM.

5 · Adaptive spreading

Switch between 31, 63 and 127 chips by measured SNR, trading rate for range beyond what adaptive modulation already does.

6 · Orthogonal codes inside a slot

Walsh codes under a scrambling code for the chip-aligned bursts of one slot, removing the 29.4 / 25.3 dB inter-code floor and opening the way to 64-QAM ⅚ (~19 dB).

7 · Multi-hop relaying

Routes over several relays. Today a message takes at most one hop, through a station that hears both ends; a station two hops away is out of reach.

8 · Per-pair keys

X25519 keys in the beacons instead of one shared passphrase, for forward secrecy and per-pair privacy.

9 · More stations

Add code lanes to the flowgraph (one copy of a lane per station); the Gold family has 33 codes.

10 · Analog power control

Set the ANTSDR's attenuator per slot, so lower power also lowers the transmitter's noise floor and LO leakage.

11 · Cleaner network merges

Let the yielding network stay silent until its stations have joined, so a merge never overlaps slots.

12 · Games

Hands encrypted per player, a replicated move log for host handover, spectators and computer players.

13 · Fragments that fit an idle slot

Cut a message of a few fragments into pieces that fit the sender's idle slot at its current rate (about 600 bytes with four stations), or make idle slots one full frame long while three or four stations are on the air, so that a message of a few kilobytes starts at once instead of 1.4 s later.

14 · Grow the relay's slot with the sender's

A sender knows when its message goes through a relay; its header could ask for the relay's airtime too, so both slots grow in one plan change, and its ACK timer could allow for the relay's queue. Relayed transfers would start 2–3 s sooner.
